figures.label: fig:v9-rank-matrix-chart
figures.title: Near a matrix with an invertible $r\times r$ minor $A$, rank $r$ forces $D=CA^{-1}B$. The blocks $A,B,C$ are free coordinates; $D$ is determined. Their total number of entries is $r^2+r(n-r)+(m-r)r=r(m+n-r)$. Exercise~\ref {ex:v9-rank-matrix-chart} proves the chart and its tangent-space formula

figures.label: fig:v9-critical-image
figures.title: For $f(x,y)=(x,y^2)$, the square $[-h,h]^2$ maps onto $[-h,h]\times [0,h^2]$. The panels use the same axis scale, with $h=1/2$. The source area is $4h^2$ and the image area $2h^3$; their ratio tends to zero with $h$. The critical diameter $y=0$ maps to a line segment

figures.label: fig:v9-ch02-escape-times
figures.title: For $x'=x^2$, the initial values $1$ and $-1$ give $x(t)=1/(1-t)$ and $x(t)=-1/(1+t)$. Their maximal intervals end at $1$ and begin at $-1$, respectively; the zero solution is stationary for every time. The dashed lines mark the endpoints excluded from those respective time intervals

figures.label: fig:v9-ch02-flow-coordinates
figures.title: The commuting fields $X=\partial _x$ and $Y=y\partial _x+\partial _y$ become coordinate fields under $u=x-y^2/2$, $v=y$. Straight $u,v$ grid lines map to horizontal lines and parabolas in the original plane

figures.label: fig:v9-ch03-pullback-area
figures.title: The map $(s,t)\mapsto (2s+t,t)$ takes the unit square to a parallelogram of area $2$. Pullback records the same factor: $(2\dd s+\dd t)\wedge \dd t=2\dd s\wedge \dd t$

figures.label: fig:v9-ch03-vector-potential
figures.title: For a constant upward field $F=(0,0,1)$, the radial primitive gives $A=(-y/2,x/2,0)$, tangent to horizontal circles with length $r/2$ at radius $r$. Counterclockwise circulation around a radius-$R$ circle is $\pi R^2$, matching upward flux through the disk

figures.label: fig:v9-ch04-stereographic-length
figures.title: For the spherical metric $4(dx^2+dy^2)/(1+r^2)^2$, the coordinate circle of radius $r$ has length $4\pi r/(1+r^2)$. Its greatest length is $2\pi $ at $r=1$; very large coordinate circles approach the omitted pole and shrink in spherical length

figures.label: fig:v9-ch04-frequency-circles
figures.title: Each lattice point is one square-torus Fourier mode. The circles $|k|^2=1,2,4$ each contain four lattice points, hence give eigenvalues $4\pi ^2$, $8\pi ^2$, $16\pi ^2$ of multiplicity four. The origin gives the one-dimensional zero eigenspace

figures.label: fig:v9-three-sheet-cover
figures.title: A three-sheeted cover of the figure eight. The $a$-edges cycle $1\to 2\to 3\to 1$, while the $b$-edges exchange $1,2$ and fix $3$. Each label has one incoming and one outgoing edge at every vertex. A symmetry of the covering must preserve both permutations; only the identity does. Exercise~\ref {ex:v9-three-sheet-cover} computes its subgroup

figures.label: fig:v9-shrinking-circles
figures.title: The circles with centres $(1/n,0)$ and radii $1/n$ all pass through $0$. Only the first few are drawn. Every neighbourhood of $0$ contains whole circles, however small it is; each such circle still detects a nontrivial loop. Exercise~\ref {ex:v9-shrinking-circles} uses this to rule out a simply connected covering

figures.label: fig:v9-filled-cycle
figures.title: The same oriented three-edge cycle in two spaces. On the left it generates $H_1\cong \Z $; on the right it is the boundary $\partial [0,1,2]=[1,2]-[0,2]+[0,1]$ of the filled triangle, so its class is zero. Homology asks what bounds inside the space

figures.label: fig:v9-local-stars
figures.title: Remove the central vertex of a small star. One, two and three arms leave one, two and three components. The local relative $H_1$ groups are consequently $0$, $\Z $ and $\Z ^2$. This distinguishes an interval endpoint, an interior point and a branch point; see Exercise~\ref {ex:v9-local-homology}

figures.label: fig:v9-spin-lift
figures.title: A full-turn loop in $SO(3)$ lifts from $I$ to $-I$ in $SU(2)$; a second turn closes the lift. The upper and lower paths are schematic parameter paths, not distances in the groups. The endpoints have the same spatial rotation but different points of the covering sphere

figures.label: fig:v9-affine-product
figures.title: The affine maps $T(x)=x+1$ and $D(x)=2x$ do not commute: $D(T(0))=2$ while $T(D(0))=1$. Their matrices lie in a two-dimensional Lie group. The order of the arrows records composition; the bracket of its dilation and translation directions is a translation direction

figures.label: fig:v9-jacobian-square
figures.title: For $j=1,k=2,t_1=1,t_2=i$, the Jacobian multiplies the complex coordinate $K_{12}$ by $i-1$. A unit square of area one becomes a diamond of area two, exactly $|t_2-t_1|^2$. Each off-diagonal pair is a real two-dimensional plane, which produces the square in the Vandermonde weight

figures.label: fig:v9-count-variance
figures.title: For two points and an arc occupying a fraction $p$ of the circle, independent sampling gives count variance $2p(1-p)$. Haar $U(2)$ eigenvalues give $2p-2p^2-2(\sin (\pi p)/\pi )^2$, the lower curve. The calculation in Exercise~\ref {ex:v9-arc-variance} measures more even counts without claiming that every individual configuration is evenly spaced

figures.label: fig:v9-ch09-geodesic-horocycle
figures.title: At $i$, the geodesic flow moves upward along $ie^t$. The horocycle flow moves horizontally along $s+i$ while carrying the upward unit normal. The carried vector is not the horocycle's tangent

figures.label: fig:v9-ch09-axis-displacement
figures.title: For $z\mapsto e^\ell z$, the imaginary axis attains the minimum displacement $\ell $. At the same height, moving away from the axis increases $\cosh d$ by $(\cosh \ell -1)(x/y)^2$. The drawn example uses $\ell =\log 2$

figures.label: fig:v9-root-separation
figures.title: For the branch $q(z)=\sqrt {z}$ on the slit plane, the image is the right half-plane. A disc about $c=1$ in that image has its reflection about $-1$ in the missing left half-plane. In the general proof the image need not be a half-plane; only the disjointness of $q(\Omega )$ and $-q(\Omega )$ is needed

figures.label: fig:v9-extremal-map
figures.title: The missing-point argument factors $F$ through another admissible map $h$. The map $\Psi $ fixes $0$ but is not injective, because it includes squaring on the whole disc. Schwarz's lemma forces $|\Psi '(0)|<1$, so $h$ stretches more than $F$ at $z_0$

figures.label: fig:v9-ch11-window-directions
figures.title: For a rectangular window, more offsets hit when its projection onto the line normal is wider. Conditional on a hit, the normal-angle density is proportional to $a|\cos \theta |+b|\sin \theta |$, so uniformly choosing an angle and then a hitting offset gives a different law in general

figures.label: fig:v9-ch11-spherical-incidence
figures.title: A great circle with pole $u$ meets the latitude boundary at colatitude $a$ precisely when $|u\cdot n|\le \sin a$. On the pole sphere this is an equatorial band. Its area fraction is $\sin a$, and almost every hitting great circle has two boundary intersections. The example has $a=\pi /6$

figures.label: fig:v9-orthic-unfolding
figures.title: At the orthic triangle in this acute equilateral example, reflecting the altitude foot $D$ across $AB,AC$ gives $D',D''$. The straight route $D'\!F\!E\!D''$ has the same length as the closed route $D\!F\!E\!D$. This verifies equality for the minimizing configuration; no such side-intersection claim is needed for arbitrary $D$

figures.label: fig:v9-fivefold-obstruction
figures.title: If a plane lattice had a $72^\circ $ rotation and a shortest nonzero vector $v$ of length $\delta $, then $v+\rho ^2v$ would be a nonzero lattice vector of length $2\delta \cos 72^\circ <\delta $. It lies inside the dashed shortest-length circle, a contradiction. The other marked orbit points are hypothetical lattice points under that assumption

figures.label: fig:v9-descartes-line
figures.title: The tangent-circle curvatures $1,1,4,12$ satisfy Descartes' relation. Replacing the curvature-$12$ member gives curvature zero: the common tangent line $y=-1$, not a circle with a finite centre. Exercise~\ref {ex:v9-descartes-line} computes its normalized coefficient vector

figures.label: fig:v9-sphere-image-charge
figures.title: A meridional cross-section of a sphere of radius $R=1$. A source at $P=(2,0)$ has inverse point $P'=(1/2,0)$. At each sphere point $Q$, $|Q-P'|=|Q-P|/2$. A charge of strength $-1/2$ at $P'$ therefore cancels the source potential on the whole sphere; Exercise~\ref {ex:v9-sphere-image-charge} verifies the three-dimensional derivatives and flux

figures.label: fig:v9-dual-pappus
figures.title: Two pencils at $U,V$. Write $P_1=a\cap b'$, $P_2=a'\cap b$, $Q_1=a\cap c'$, $Q_2=a'\cap c$, $R_1=b\cap c'$, $R_2=b'\cap c$. The three coral joining lines meet at $K$: the dual of Pappus

figures.label: fig:v9-two-perspectivities
figures.title: Two central projections take $X\in L$ to $Y\in N$ and then to $Z\in M$. Here $L:y=0$, $M:x=0$, $N:y=x+1$, with centres $O_1=(1,1)$ and $O_2=(-1,-2)$. The composite need not fix $S=L\cap M$

figures.label: fig:v9-pell-parametrization
figures.title: A line of slope $t$ through $P=(0,1)$ meets $y^2=2x^2+1$ again at a rational point when $t$ is rational. The displayed choice $t=1$ gives $(2,3)$. The vertical parameter gives $(0,-1)$; the tangent parameter $t=0$ returns $P$

figures.label: fig:v9-fuss-kite
figures.title: A symmetric Poncelet quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $AC$ a diameter. At $B$ the two tangents are perpendicular. Their unit-normal components give $r^2/(R-d)^2+r^2/(R+d)^2=1$, Fuss's condition. Here $R=1$, $d=3/10$, $r=91/(10\sqrt {218})$

figures.label: geometry:fig:v9-polarisation
figures.title: For $q(x,y)=x^2+y^2$, the mixed difference $q(u+v)-q(u)-q(v)$ is twice the dot product. Here $u=(2,0)$ and $v=(1,1)$ give $10-4-2=4=2(u\cdot v)$. The dashed segments construct the vector sum

figures.label: geometry:fig:v9-projective-grid
figures.title: The two ruling coordinates of a hyperbolic quadric over $\mathbb F_3$ form a $4\times 4$ array. Each dot represents one point $\sigma (a,b)$; each row and each column represents a projective line with four points. Same-family lines are disjoint; a row and a column meet in one point. The array records incidence, not a Euclidean embedding

figures.label: fig:v9-cusp-multiplicity
figures.title: The cusp $y^2=x^3$ and the secant $y=x$ meet with orders two at $(0,0)$ and one at $(1,1)$. The tangent $y=0$ instead puts all three orders at the cusp. A line missing the tangent direction need not have order one at a singular point

figures.label: fig:v9-grid-weights
figures.title: Weights on the grid $\{-1,0,1\}^2$. For any polynomial $H$ of total degree at most three, the weighted sum of its nine values is zero. The last value is consequently determined by the other eight. The formula is derived from elementary interpolation in Exercise~\ref {ex:v9-grid-interpolation}

figures.label: fig:v9-modular-chord
figures.title: Addition on $y^2=x^3+x+1$ over $\mathbb F_5$. The modular line $y=4x+1$ contains $P=(0,1)$, $Q=(4,2)$ and $R=(2,4)$ on the curve. Reflecting $R$ modulo five gives $P+Q=(2,1)$. The broken drawing reflects reduction modulo five; the line is not one ordinary Euclidean segment in this grid

figures.label: fig:v9-hesse-pencil
figures.title: Over $\C $, the Hesse pencil is $X^3+Y^3+Z^3-3\kappa XYZ=0$. The three finite parameters $1,\omega ,\omega ^2$ with $\omega $ a primitive cube root of unity give triangles, as does the member $XYZ=0$ at infinity. All members share nine coordinate-line basepoints. The remaining members are smooth, with these nine points as their flexes

figures.label: geometry:fig:v9-folding
figures.title: Blichfeldt's overlap step for $\Z ^2$. Two small pieces lie in adjacent unit cells. Translating the rust piece by $-(1,0)$ into the half-open fundamental square makes it overlap the charcoal piece. A set of area greater than one forces an overlap somewhere, even when its pieces have different shapes

figures.label: geometry:fig:v9-basis-reduction
figures.title: Subtracting twice $u=(1,0)$ from $v=(2.4,1)$ gives $v'=(0.4,1)$. The rust and charcoal parallelograms have the same area, one, and generate the same lattice. The new basis is reduced: $|u|\le |v'|$ and $|u\cdot v'|=0.4\le 0.5$

figures.label: geometry:fig:v9-polar-circles
figures.title: In the Poincar\'e disc, circles at hyperbolic distances $r=0.5,1,2,3$ from $0$ have Euclidean radii $\tanh (r/2)$. Their Euclidean spacing shrinks towards the boundary while their hyperbolic circumference $2\pi \sinh r$ grows. The dashed boundary is not part of the plane

figures.label: geometry:fig:v9-triangle-area
figures.title: A fan from one vertex divides a convex hyperbolic pentagon into three triangles. Summing their areas gives $3\pi $ minus the sum of the pentagon's interior angles. The drawn pentagon is in the Klein disc, where h-lines appear straight; its Euclidean angles do not represent hyperbolic angles

figures.label: fig:v9-app-j-helly-sharp
figures.title: The three edges of a triangle meet in pairs, but all three have no common point. Convexity alone cannot lower Helly's planar requirement from three sets to two

figures.label: fig:v9-app-j-parallel-body
figures.title: Adding a radius-$\varepsilon $ disk to a rectangle adds four side strips and four quarter-disks. Their areas give $A+L\varepsilon +\pi \varepsilon ^2$; the same decomposition uses exterior-angle sectors for a general polygon

figures.label: fig:v9-app-k-turning-offset
figures.title: For a circle of radius $R$, the left unit normal points inward. The offset $\gamma +aN$ has radius $R-a$ and curvature $1/(R-a)$ for $0\le a<R$. At $a=R$ the whole curve collapses and its parametrization is no longer regular

figures.label: fig:v9-app-k-pyramid-defect
figures.title: An $n$-gonal pyramid with unit slant edges has apex face angle $\alpha _n=2\arcsin (\sin \beta \sin (\pi /n))$. The unfolded face angles leave a gap $2\pi -n\alpha _n$, which tends to $2\pi (1-\sin \beta )$ as the pyramid approaches a cone
